WHY ANDES HVAC
Why Choose Us

Six reasons homeowners across Montclair, Ridgewood, Summit and the rest of North Jersey keep calling us back.

Existing Buildings Only

We service, repair and replace equipment in homes and buildings that are already standing and lived in. No new construction, no rough-ins — just the systems people are relying on today.

We Diagnose Before We Quote

Gauges on the ports, amp draw measured, controls checked in order. Finding the actual fault is what stops a thirty-dollar part turning into a whole new system.

Honest, Up-Front Pricing

Free estimates and the price for the repair before the work starts. Ask about 15% off your next maintenance service.

Open Six Days a Week

Monday to Friday 9 AM – 5 PM and Saturdays 9 AM – 2 PM, which is usually the easiest time for someone to actually be home.

Repair or Replace, Both Priced

If a unit is worth fixing we fix it. If it is finished, we say so and price the replacement — both numbers, side by side, so the choice is yours.

Cooling and Heating, One Call

Central air, boilers, mini-splits and full unit replacement under one roof. No separate contractor for the half of the year you are not using.

GOT QUESTIONS?
Frequently Asked Questions
What areas does Andes HVAC serve?
We work across North Jersey — Montclair, Upper Montclair, Glen Ridge, Short Hills, Livingston, North Caldwell, Essex Fells, Roseland, Cedar Grove, Rutherford, Lyndhurst, Ridgewood, Glen Rock, Wyckoff, Paramus, Wayne, Summit, Westfield, Cranford and Scotch Plains, plus the towns in between. We're based in Kearny. If you're not sure whether you're in range, call and ask.
Do you work on new construction?
No. We work exclusively on existing homes and buildings — service and repair on equipment that's already in place. That's a deliberate choice: a house that's already finished and lived in is a completely different job from a rough-in, and it's the one we're set up to do well.
What does a repair cost?
It depends entirely on what has failed. A capacitor is a small job; a compressor or a heat exchanger is not. We diagnose the system first, then give you the price for the repair before any work starts — and if the unit isn't worth repairing, we'll tell you that instead of charging you to find out slowly. Estimates are free.
What does the in-person evaluation cost?
Nothing. Coming out to look at the system, work out what's wrong, and write up a price for the repair costs nothing — there's no trip charge, service call fee, or diagnostic fee added to the bill afterwards. We tell you what we found and what the fix costs before any work starts, and you decide then. If the unit turns out not to be worth repairing, we'll say so, and you haven't paid anything to find that out.
What hours are you open?
Monday through Friday, 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM, and Saturdays from 9:00 AM to 2:00 PM. Saturday appointments are often the easiest time for people to be home and walk us through what the system has been doing.
Do you offer any discount?
Yes — 15% off your next maintenance service. Refer a friend or neighbor and the same 15% applies again. Most of our work comes from word of mouth, so we'd rather put it there than into advertising.
Should I repair my air conditioner or replace it?
The honest test is age against the cost of the repair. Under about ten years old with a normal repair, fix it. Fifteen years or more with a major component gone — compressor, coil, heat exchanger — and you're usually paying a large share of a new system to extend an old one. Systems still running R-22 refrigerant tip the math toward replacement faster, because the refrigerant itself is now expensive. We'll price both and let you decide.
My house has no ductwork. Can I still get air conditioning?
Yes, and this is a lot of what we do in towns like Montclair, Glen Ridge, Rutherford and Ridgewood. A ductless mini-split puts an indoor head in the room itself and runs a small refrigerant line back to an outdoor unit, so nothing has to be opened up for duct chases. One head handles a room or an open floor; a multi-zone system handles several with one outdoor unit.
Why is my upstairs so much hotter than downstairs?
Usually it's airflow rather than capacity. Undersized or crushed returns, a clogged filter, leaking duct in a hot attic, or dampers that were never balanced will all starve the top floor while the first floor over-cools. That's worth checking before anyone sells you a bigger system. If the ductwork genuinely can't serve the floor, one ductless head upstairs fixes it permanently and costs far less than replacing everything.
Do you repair boilers as well as air conditioning?
Yes — gas and oil, steam and hot water. No heat, no hot water, banging pipes, cold rooms at the end of the loop, pressure that won't hold. Most heating failures turn out to be a control, a circulator pump, a zone valve, or air in the system rather than the boiler itself, which is why we test before we quote.
How often should I have the system serviced?
Once a year for each side: cooling in the spring, heating in the fall. It isn't a sales line — most of the emergency calls we get in July and January are for something that would have been visible and cheap during a maintenance visit. Returning customers get 15% off that service.

About Andes HVAC

An HVAC repair company serving North Jersey — six days a week, on buildings that already exist.

OUR STORY
We fix what's already there

Andes HVAC is built on a simple promise: show up when we said we would, find out what is actually wrong before quoting anything, and leave the property the way we found it. We have grown almost entirely by word of mouth across Montclair, Ridgewood, Summit, Westfield and the rest of North Jersey — one satisfied neighbor at a time.

We work exclusively on existing homes and buildings. That is a deliberate choice, not a limitation. A house that is already finished and lived in is a completely different job from a rough-in on a new build: the ductwork is where it is, the line set has to be routed through finished walls, the boiler sits where a boiler has sat for eighty years, and nobody wants their ceilings opened up. That is the work we are set up to do, and doing only that is why we are good at it.

Today we handle central air conditioning repair, gas and oil boiler repair on steam and hot-water systems, mini-split repair and installation, and rooftop AC repair. We are open Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 5 PM, and Saturdays 9 AM to 2 PM, and every estimate is free.

What We Stand For
Reliability

We show up on the day we said, at the time we said. If something moves the schedule, you hear it from us first.

Respect

It's your home. We put covers down, work clean around the mechanical room, and take the old equipment away with us.

Diagnose, Don't Guess

Gauges on the ports, amp draw measured, controls checked in order. No parts replaced hopefully and billed anyway.

Community

We live here too. We work local, and our reputation travels by word of mouth rather than advertising.

Our Mission

Keep North Jersey homes comfortable through both halves of the year, on the equipment they already have, for as long as that equipment is worth keeping. Treat every customer like a neighbor, because most of them are. Earn the next referral with the work itself.

Our Promise

We'll tell you honestly whether a unit is worth repairing — including when the answer costs us the bigger job. And if you're not happy with the work, tell us and we'll come back and make it right. That's how we've built a customer list that runs almost entirely on referrals.

Ready to Work With Us?

Get a free, no-pressure estimate on an air conditioning repair, a boiler that has stopped, a mini-split install, or a rooftop unit that will not run.

Boiler Repair

Steam and hot-water heat, kept running through winter

FREE ESTIMATE
NORTH JERSEY · MON – SAT

A lot of North Jersey heat still comes from a boiler, and much of it is older than the people living with it. We repair gas and oil-fired boilers on both steam and hot-water systems — no heat, no hot water, short cycling, banging pipes, cold rooms at the far end of the loop, pressure that will not hold. Most of what goes wrong is a control, a pump, a valve, or air in the system rather than the boiler itself, and finding that out first is what keeps a repair from turning into a replacement you did not need.

Our Process
1
Get Heat On

On a no-heat call the first job is getting the system running safely, then working out why it stopped.

2
Test the Controls

Aquastat, thermostat, pump, zone valves and safeties get checked in order, not swapped at random.

3
Repair

We replace what actually failed and correct the pressure, the venting or the air that caused it.

4
Balance & Check

The system is cycled, the zones are proved, and we confirm every room is getting heat before we go.

What's Included
No-heat and no-hot-water calls on gas and oil boilers
Circulator pumps, zone valves and thermostats
Aquastats, gas valves, ignitors and control boards
Low-water cutoffs, sight glasses and steam vents
Expansion tanks, pressure faults and system bleeding
Radiator and baseboard balancing for cold rooms
Ready to Book?

Get your free, no-pressure estimate today. Existing homes and buildings only — we don't take new construction.
